title: Property tax capitalization and local fiscal capacity: evidence from Korean housing markets (Kang & Yoon, Applied Economics Letters, online 16 Sept 2026)
what_was_fetched: Bibliographic metadata and the 15-entry reference list only, via Crossref (200) and OpenAlex (200). The abstract and full text were NOT obtained. Taylor & Francis returned a Cloudflare challenge (HTTP 403) on the DOI, /abs, /full and /pdf routes with a browser user-agent and with a Googlebot user-agent; r.jina.ai returned the same challenge page (and a 401 for the /abs route); Unpaywall reports the article closed-access with no repository copy; Crossref carries no abstract; OpenAlex carries no abstract inverted index; Semantic Scholar abstract is null; WebSearch and WebFetch did not surface the abstract. No SSRN/RePEc/university-repository working-paper version was found. Author standing was checked from OpenAlex author records (not from the paper). Files in scratch dir: i1_crossref.json, i1_unpaywall.json, i1_openalex.json, i1_doi.html (challenge page).
verdict: DEFER — no finding from this paper can be stated yet. The queue's guidance (NEW if full text, ENRICH from the abstract otherwise) cannot be met because not even the abstract was reachable. Recommended path: T1 (or a human with institutional access) pulls the abstract; if it states a capitalization estimate and a fiscal-capacity moderator, ENRICH concepts/tax-capitalization.md (one sentence plus Sources entry in the 'Evidence' list, as the first East Asian estimate beside Oates, Palmon & Smith, Borge & Rattsø, Buettner, Tubío-Sánchez & Reyes-Bueno) and places/south-korea.md (a sentence in 'The existing tax structure his reforms operate on', tying the paper to the jongbusae/local-property-tax structure already described there). A NEW research page is not warranted for a 5-page Letter unless the full text is read AND shows a clean identification strategy; if so, tier Supplementary. Do not write any number, sign, or data description from this brief: none was seen.
claim_grade: D for any substantive claim until the abstract/text is read (nothing about findings was seen). Source tier under §4c: Tier 1 — peer-reviewed in Applied Economics Letters (Taylor & Francis; a short-format letters journal, 5 pages per Crossref, so a lighter evidentiary weight than a full article); first author Sung Hoon Kang is a professor in the Department of Policy Studies, Hanyang University (OpenAlex: 20 works, h-index 6, topics 'Local Government Finance and Decentralization', 'Housing Market and Economics', 'Taxation and Compliance' — a bona fide local-fiscal-policy scholar, modest record); second author Sung-Joo Yoon, School of Economics, Chonnam National University (OpenAlex: 9 works, h-index 1; prior output is on household income mobility, e.g. Applied Economics Letters 2024, not property tax). Judged by the rubric: qualifies as an established academic source at the 'peer-reviewed paper by affiliated academics' level, not at the Oates/Zodrow level; fine for an empirical B-claim, not for 'prominent authority' framing.
content_summary: Confirmed metadata only: authors Sung Hoon Kang (Hanyang University, Seoul) and Sung-Joo Yoon (Chonnam National University, Gwangju); Applied Economics Letters, published online 2026-09-16, pages 1-5 (Crossref), Informa UK Limited; 15 references, 0 citations so far. The reference list (Crossref) shows the intellectual frame: Oates 1969 (JPE, 10.1086/259584), Tiebout 1956 (JPE, 10.1086/257839), Hamilton 1976 (AER, 'Capitalization of Intrajurisdictional Differences in Local Tax Prices'), Zodrow & Mieszkowski 1986 (JUE 19(3), 'Pigou, Tiebout, property taxation, and the underprovision of local public goods', 10.1016/0094-1190(86)90048-3 — this confirms the queue note that it cites Zodrow-Mieszkowski), Livy 2018 (JHE, intra-school-district capitalization of property tax rates), Elinder & Persson 2017 (JEBO, house price responses to the Swedish national property tax reform), Oliviero & Scognamiglio 2019 (EER, 2012 Italian property tax reform), Lyu 2024 (RSUE, 'Revisiting property tax capitalization'), Bradley 2017 (REStat, Michigan assessment lags), Avenancio-León & Howard 2022 (QJE, assessment gap). Eight of the fifteen references are therefore on-topic. The other references are not on-topic: four are by or with Değirmenci (sustainable development, green budget, East African Community tax capacity) and one is a panel-ARDL exchange-rate paper (Ramos-Herrera 2024) — a pattern a T1 may read as reference padding; it does not by itself bear on the paper's validity but is worth noting when weighing it. Data (which Korean housing prices and years), which property tax (jongbusae vs the local property tax), identification, the capitalization estimate, the fiscal-capacity interaction and the policy conclusion: NOT KNOWN. Unattributed lead only: a 2013 Korean study (Creative Education/Scirp 'Current Urban Studies', doi 10.4236/cus.2013.14012, 'The Estimation of Property Tax Capitalisation in the Korean Taxation Context') reportedly estimated Seoul apartment capitalization at 73.7-82.8% by repeat sales (WebSearch snippet, not fetched or checked; low-tier publisher) — a possible Korean baseline for T1 to check, not a claim to publish.
existing_wiki_coverage: concepts/tax-capitalization.md (last_reviewed 2026-07-06) already carries the Oates 1969, Palmon & Smith 1998, Høj-Jørgensen-Schou 2017 (Denmark, full capitalization), Borge & Rattsø (Norway), Buettner (Germany), Falkenbach et al. 2026 (Helsinki lease), and Tubío-Sánchez & Reyes-Bueno (Ecuador) evidence; it has no Korean or other East Asian estimate. Theory pages exist for the frame the paper uses: research/oates-1969-capitalization.md (full), research/hamilton-benefit-tax.md, research/zodrow-three-views.md, research/mieszkowski-property-tax-incidence.md, concepts/tiebout-model.md, research/hilber-capitalization-synthesis.md — so a one-line enrichment can link the benefit-view/capital-tax-view context internally without new theory text. places/south-korea.md (last_reviewed 2026-08-16) covers KLC/LH public land development, Lee Jae-myung's land-dividend politics, the July 2026 National Assembly Budget Office comparison (Korea alone in levying both a local property tax at 0.05-0.4% and the national comprehensive real estate tax, jongbusae, at 0.5-5.0%), and the August 2026 jongbusae reform; it has no academic empirical evidence on property-tax effects on Korean prices. No wiki page covers Lyu 2024, Elinder & Persson 2017, Oliviero & Scognamiglio 2019, Livy 2018 or Bradley 2017 (grep of the digest and repo found none), which are candidate sources for the same enrichment if T1 wants wider coverage.
uncertainties: (1) Everything about the paper's findings. (2) Which Korean tax it studies is unknown: the title says 'property tax' and 'local fiscal capacity', which suggests the local property tax (jaesanse), but the jongbusae is the policy-salient one the wiki page describes; do not assume. (3) 'Local fiscal capacity' may enter as a moderator, a mediator or a control; do not write 'fiscal capacity modifies capitalization' without reading the abstract. (4) The Zodrow-Mieszkowski benefit-view/capital-tax-view framing is inferred from the reference list, not from the text. (5) OpenAlex author metrics were read once; the author-level queries for paper lists hit a rate limit, so the authors' prior property-tax record was not enumerated. Kang's OpenAlex topics are consistent with the subject; Yoon's are health/statistics, so a T1 should not cite Yoon's standing for the property-tax claim. (6) The paper's page count (5) suggests a narrow result; weight accordingly.

title: Fixation of Ceiling Limits on Land Holdings under the Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Act, 1961 (Srevel Arvind, SSRN preprint, posted 18 Sept 2026)
what_was_fetched: The paper's full text was NOT obtained. SSRN returned a Cloudflare challenge (HTTP 403) for papers.cfm and Delivery.cfm on both deposits (7476999 and the duplicate 7477002), with browser and Googlebot user-agents; r.jina.ai returned the challenge page. What was obtained: the full author-supplied abstract (identical on both deposits) and metadata from Crossref; the author's ORCID record (public API); an OpenAlex record. Also fetched, to give T1 primary-source anchors independent of the preprint: the 1961 Act's consolidated text as hosted by PRS Legislative Research (169 pages, OCR text parsed with pymupdf; PRS states its copy is not authoritative). Besley & Burgess bibliographic data checked via Crossref. Files in scratch dir: i2_cr_7476999.json, i2_cr_7477002.json, act.pdf, act.txt (OCR text; noisy), plus the challenge pages.
verdict: REJECT as a source — a Tier 2 solo preprint (author is a law student; see claim_grade) with zero cited references on Crossref and no traceable Tier 1 lead. It adds nothing the Act's own text and the Tier 1 literature do not give better. NOTE FOR LATER, not for this batch: the wiki has no coverage whatsoever of India's land-ceiling laws or of Indian land reform generally (the only India pages are land-pooling/Gujarat TPS, MoHUA value capture, Sampat on rentier growth infrastructure, the Chennai property-tax RCT, Telangana CURE bill, and the 2024 mineral-royalty ruling). If the editor wants that gap filled, the page should be built from Tier 1 sources: (a) the Act itself (India Code / Government of Tamil Nadu Land Reforms department, landreforms.tn.gov.in) with its amendments; (b) Timothy Besley & Robin Burgess (2000), 'Land Reform, Poverty Reduction, and Growth: Evidence from India', Quarterly Journal of Economics 115(2): 389-430, DOI 10.1162/003355300554809 — not currently in the wiki (the repo mentions Besley only as a Mirrlees Review co-author); (c) official land-reform statistics (Ministry of Rural Development / Department of Land Resources, Planning Commission and NITI Aayog reports) for surplus declared and distributed; (d) Supreme Court decisions on the Ninth Schedule and Article 31A. A Georgist angle (land concentration, taxation versus ceilings as instruments) would need an authored link to LVT, which the abstract does not supply.
claim_grade: D — Tier 2 under §4c. Author: Srevel Arvind (OpenAlex displays 'M.A. Srevel Arvind'). The author's ORCID record (0009-0005-3416-4278) is self-registered, created September 2026, and lists a single employment entry: role 'Student', Tamil Nadu Dr. Ambedkar Law University (department string 'S Thangazgam Law college'), Chennai, start 2026-09. No prior publications, no affiliation on the SSRN deposit (Crossref affiliation empty), Crossref reference-count 0. The paper is a doctrinal law-student exercise, not peer-reviewed. Standing cannot be verified at Tier 1; do not cite as support for anything. The two Act-level facts below that appear in this brief are sourced to the Act's text, not to the preprint.
content_summary: From the author's abstract (the only part of the paper read): doctrinal and analytical methodology using statutes, constitutional provisions, case law and legal commentaries; traces the historical and constitutional background of land reform in India and Tamil Nadu; explains the statutory concept of ceiling; examines machinery for determining holdings, identifying surplus land, taking possession and distributing it; attends to family holdings, standard acres, exemptions, transfers made to defeat the ceiling (sham transfers), protected tenants and the role of competent authorities; discusses Articles 14, 31A and 300A of the Constitution; analyses judicial decisions balancing legislative aims with procedural fairness and property interests; concludes that ceiling legislation remains significant as a redistributive instrument but depends on accurate land records, transparent proceedings, timely adjudication, prevention of sham transfers and fair implementation, and recommends administrative and procedural reforms. The abstract states no figures, case names, or statistics, so the ceiling number, the exemptions, the litigation record and any effect-size evidence that the queue asked for are NOT available from the preprint and its list of Tier 1 citations is unknown (Crossref shows no references). Independent primary-source anchors from the Act text (PRS copy, OCR; for T1 to confirm against India Code): s.5(1) sets the ceiling area at 15 standard acres for a family of not more than five members, and under s.5(1)(b) a family of more than five members gets 15 standard acres plus 5 standard acres for each member beyond five; the footnotes record that the figure was originally 30 standard acres and was cut to 15 by the Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Reduction of Ceiling on Land) Act, 1970 (T.N. Act 17 of 1970, deemed in force 15 Feb 1970) and restated by the Third Amendment Act, 1972 (T.N. Act 37 of 1972, in force 1 Mar 1972); s.5(1)(c) gives institutional ceilings (college 40 standard acres, high school 20, elementary school 10, students' hostel 25) and s.5(1)(d) gives public charitable trusts 5 standard acres; the contents list shows the surplus mechanism as returns and draft statements (ss.8-12), a final statement, and notification of surplus land vesting in Government (s.18, with later ss.18-A to 18-F) and compensation under Chapter-level provisions. These are the Act's provisions as printed in an unofficial OCR copy; amounts and section numbers must be checked against India Code before use. The standard-acre conversion (land classified by yield) was not extracted.
existing_wiki_coverage: None on India's land-ceiling laws, the Tamil Nadu Act, Indian land reform, or Besley & Burgess. Related pages the digest holds: research/india-mohua-value-capture-framework.md (its own text notes broader property-tax history, land reform and Georgist reception 'remains an open gap'), concepts/land-pooling.md (Gujarat Town Planning Schemes), research/sampat-india-rentier-growth-infrastructure.md (Sampat, Antipode 2025: Dholera and Goa SEZ land appropriation; page itself rests on an abstract-level secondary reconstruction, and concerns post-liberalization growth infrastructure, not ceilings), research/commander-estrin-india-business-groups.md, research/duflo-hanna-olken-tandon-chennai-outsourcing.md (Chennai property-tax RCT, the only Tamil Nadu-linked page), events/2024-india-mineral-royalty-tax-ruling.md (mentions India Cement v. State of Tamil Nadu, a royalty case unrelated to ceilings), events/telangana-cure-bill-hyderabad.md. The closest conceptual neighbour is events/taiwan-land-reform-1950s.md (land-to-the-tiller; cites Lam & Tsui 1998 via Lincoln Institute and Kim & Wang 2025) — a ceiling-and-redistribution case that the wiki does hold, and the natural comparison page for any future Indian land-reform page. The Sampat page is unrelated to this item and should not be cross-linked as if it were.
uncertainties: (1) The preprint body was never read: all 'what the paper says' comes from a 200-word abstract. (2) Whether the 17-page paper cites any Tier 1 source (Besley & Burgess, Supreme Court or Madras High Court judgments, government statistics) is unknown; the empty Crossref reference list does not prove the PDF has no bibliography, because SSRN deposits often omit reference metadata. A T1 with access could open the PDF to see its bibliography, but the author-tier rule still makes the paper itself non-citable. (3) The ceiling figures above come from the OCR of PRS's copy of a heavily amended Act; the present-day text may have further amendments (including the Ninth Schedule status and later Tamil Nadu amendments) and the 'family' definition was not checked. (4) The Besley & Burgess finding on ceiling legislation was not re-read in this pass; from memory its headline result concerns tenancy reform and abolition of intermediaries associated with poverty reduction, with ceilings and consolidation less clearly so — treat that as unchecked and read the paper before using it. (5) The duplicate deposit 7477002 (posted 2026-09-19) has the same abstract and author; only 7476999 is queued; if anything were ever cited, the DOI choice would need deciding, but the verdict is reject. (6) Georgist relevance is thin: land ceilings are a quantity-restriction redistribution tool, distinct from rent capture by taxation; Georgists' own comparison of the two is a separate argument the abstract does not make.
